The material used in the present study was a new designed alloy with the nominal composition of Ti-2Al-9.2Mo-2Fe (wt.%). The alloy was melted by double VAR (Vacuum Are Remelting) processing. The ingot after homogenization at 1100°C for 1 hour was broken down and forged to the square billets with 380 mm in each dimension. The square billets were then hot rolled at 800°C into the round bars with 12 mm in diameter.

For grain growth study, the samples from the as-rolled alloy were isothermally heat-treated in a pre-heated air furnace at five different temperatures (820°C, 850°C, 900°C, 950°C, 1000°C) and kept for the time ranging from 0.5 h to 12 h.

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructures before and after heat treatment
evidence.quote: The alloy solution-treated at 820°C exhibited the slow grain growth with the increasing time. The microstructures consisted of the equiaxed β grains with the size of 40 ~ 50 μm due to recrystallization as shown in Fig. 3.

evidence.section: 3.2 Effect of temperature and time on the uniformity of β grain size
evidence.quote: The grain uniformity values ( η) for the alloy was about 0.6 when the alloy was heat-treated at lower temperatures (820°C ~ 900°C), and about 0.5 when heat-treated at higher temperatures (950°C ~ 1000°C).
The lower exponent values (n) and the higher activation energy (Q) can be attributed to the solute drag effect and the high Mo content with low diffusivity in Ti matrix.

evidence.section: 3.2 Effect of temperature and time on the uniformity of β grain size
evidence.quote: As the β grains increase in size, the grain growth is driven by the reduction in the energy associated with the decrease in grain boundary area. The grain growth occurs by the migration of grain boundaries.

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructures before and after heat treatment
evidence.quote: It seems that not all the grains can enlarge, but the large ones grow at the expense of the small ones that shrink. Thus, the average grain size increases with the holding times, and at any particular instant there will exist a range of grain sizes.

the grain growth proceeded more rapidly as temperature increased; that is, the curves were displaced upward to the larger grain sizes. This is explained by the enhancement of diffusion rate with the increasing temperature.
